text:
anya: Heads-up: after the latest runtime deploy we saw a sustained p99 rehydrate spike on a few nodes that correlates with elevated evict churn. Quick log snippet from node-17: 
```
[kvcache] evict: prefix=tenant/123 hot=true score=24.3 prefill_state=IN_PROGRESS slab_alloc_failed=true
[kvcache] prefill: prefix=tenant/123 start alloc=5/128 batches=3
[kvcache] evict: prefix=tenant/123 skipped=false reason=score_high
[kvcache] rehydrate: prefix=tenant/123 miss cause=evicted_during_prefill
```
kevin: Oof. That log implies sweep and prefill racing for the same slab. We recently reduced prefill backpressure to improve cold-starts which might have made prefills more aggressive.
samir: Two immediate approaches: 1) conservative: make prefill operations set a temporary "protected" bit on the prefix that prevents eviction until prefill completes; 2) heuristic: let eviction proceed but add anti-thrashing so a recently-prefilled prefix has a boosted residency score for a cooldown period.
liz: Protected bit is simple but scary if prefill can stall. We need an absolute bound: protected TTL, plus a watchdog that can cancel stuck prefills and clear protection.
anya: Agreed. Also we should tag prefill flows with id and origin so we can correlate which customers (hosted/dedicated/private) drive the behavior. Add metric kvcache.prefill.inflight{origin,id,prefix}.
kevin: Implementation sketch: prefill acquires a prefix_lock and sets meta.protected_until = now + min(prefill_estimated_duration, PROTECT_MAX_MS). Evict path checks protected_until > now and returns SKIP. Also emit metric kvcache.evict.skipped_protected.
samir: Alternative idea that avoids binary protected flag: introduce an eviction debt ledger per-prefix. Each prefill increments debt proportional to expected allocation. Eviction can borrow against debt up to a limit; when debt > threshold eviction is deprioritized. This integrates better with fairness since debt can be decayed by access hits.
morgan: Both sound reasonable. Which has less blast radius? The debt ledger seems more complex than we want for a quick canary. Protected bit + strict TTL + watchdog is lower-risk for a short experiment.
liz: Rollback safety: 1) protected TTL must be capped (e.g. 45s), 2) node-level global cap on protected memory (so a noisy prefill can't fill all slabs), 3) metric alarm if protected_count/node > X for > 30s.
kevin: I'll prototype protected_until with PROTECT_MAX_MS=45000 and node_protected_memory_pct=15% for the canary. Also add log lines when evict is skipped with current memory usage.
anya: I'll add dashboards: panel for kvcache.prefill.inflight by origin, kvcache.evict.skipped_protected, protected_memory_pct, and rehydrate p99. Also a debug panel showing prefix_lock wait times.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for kevin/prefill-protect-canary at 2025-03-22T14:12Z :rocket:
samir: Test plan: two synthetic workloads: A) hotkey tight-loop (single tenant hot) B) mixed-tenants (1k tenants, Zipf 1.2). Run each for 60m and compare evict churn, protected_count, p99 rehydrate, and memory headroom.
morgan: Add regression criteria: if protected_count/node > 200 for > 2m -> abort; if memory_used_pct > 85% -> abort; if p99_rehydrate improves by <5% but p50 worsens -> revert.
liz: Also include a fuzz case where prefill intentionally stalls (inject sleep) to validate watchdog clears protection and frees memory.
kevin: Noted. I'll push the spike and share PR link when ready. Expect telemetry + logs to land in ~30m.
anya: Thanks. I'll watch dashboards and post results in the thread. If numbers look good we can consider a follow-up to the debt-ledger approach for long-term fairness.
morgan: Thanks everyone. Created ticket: kvcache/prefill-protect-canary with runbook and rollback conditions.
